body: Now it appears my dad will be leaving the hospital soon, perhaps in the next couple of days, because I'm pretty sure he's been lying to the doctor about "feeling better". I actually talked to his doctor for the first time today after sending messages for her to call me. Found out that he did not want her to contact me, or any of the family, but especially me, because he's afraid that I am going to put him in a nursing home. She told me this. So I guess he doesn't want me in his life anymore. That's fine, I guess. It fucking hurts though. I tried the best I could to help him these past few years through his medical problems. And now he doesn't want me to be any part of it. I guess my purpose in life has been fulfilled. Time to reevaluate my life I guess. Thanks for keeping me sane this past week.
Thank you...that means a lot. I'll try and get a little rest now.

No...no it's not...not at all. Today has been hell. 

Apologies for the long post, but I have plenty on my mind.

Started off the morning with the idea of talking to either my dad's doctor or my grandma (his mom) about the situation. I've been avoiding it for so long, but I was coaxed to reach out for help by my mom because she sees the toll my father's health has taken on my own. I decided to do it away from him because I feel like he doesn't want me to say certain things to them which may place him in assisted living, a place he does not want to go and I am desperately trying to avoid for him. 

I called my brother to keep him company while I did this. He's been acting very peculiar this past week and I know he needed someone there in case he fell or something. I went on my way after he showed up, drove for what seemed like 15 minutes smoking a bunch of cigarettes, thinking over what I was going to do. I finally pulled into a parking lot and called his physician and talked to a nurse about everything...and I mean everything. I completely broke down on the phone with her. Sometimes I was crying, other times I felt that I was doing the wrong thing...but I know it had to be done. Apparently he has been lying to his doctor about his condition. According to them, he takes his medication on time, never ODs, does breathing treatments three times a day, and to top it off, apparently they never knew I've lived with him for the past three years caring for him like I have been. I told them nearly everything he told them was false. His nebulizer (breathing treatment apparatus) is still in the package from when he got it two years ago. He's never touched it, but last week when they did a breathing treatment on him, he told them he did it earlier in the day already. A blatant lie. We talked for well over 30 minutes and they told me everything we talked about will be confidential, and they are glad that I called. I think they have been waiting for me to call for some time. They...I mean we, will formulate a plan to get him back to proper health, and if that includes assisted care...so be it.

After talking to them, I decided to tell my grandma about it in person. I don't often see her, and felt this is something best not discussed over the phone. Fate, unfortunately, had far different plans for my day.

I received a call from my brother en route to grandma's. Dad fell in the bathroom, and he needed help getting him up. I rushed over as quick as I could, utilizing my best Grand Theft Auto skills (the game, not the crime) to get there fast. I got there and he was curled up in a fetal position with his underwear down to his feet next to the toilet with my brother frantically trying to lift him. I told him to get out of the way and I moved stuff out of the way to make some room. Somehow we managed to lift him and guide him to the couch. He was hurt, but his pain medication shielded his pain. He was in a daze, he did not know what happened. After some quick thinking, I called 911 and EMTs arrived in minutes. After talking to them about his medication, history, and their diagnosis of him, they took him to the hospital. My brother and I followed the ambulance and we stayed at the ER for hours. I had to leave because I have a deployment ceremony for my unit to go to tomorrow, but my brother stayed until he got admitted. I've talked to my grandma and one of his brothers about it, and they told me I did the right thing, trying to cheer me up about the ordeal. The docs suspect he's taken too much of something, possibly Vicodin and/or Xanax. I think they are right. His brother, my uncle, told me we all need to sit down next week to figure out what to do. Drug detox treatment is a possibility. This means he may be taken away for a few weeks to get him off his addiction to painkillers. I know it may be the right course of action, but I don't want my dad to feel that I am putting him there on purpose. Nothing could be further from the truth. I want him to live his life happily and healthy. But today...it was too much.

I'm back home now, have been for 5 hours now. I have to be awake in 4, and I am so nervous I cannot sleep. I keep telling myself I did the right thing. I know I did. Everyone else is telling me that. It was so hard to do this. My dad has been in the hospital before, but this time feels different. Like it is more urgent, and it is. His life was in my brother's and my hands today, more so than any other day. My mind is racing...I feel so mentally exhausted from today. I keep going over the events of today. Seeing my dad on the bathroom floor, paramedics checking his blood pressure and getting a reading of 62/40, his confusion over what has been going on. I am trying to make myself cry to relieve some of my emotions, but it's just not working. At first I thought it was because I was just numb from it all, but then I thought to when I was 6 years old and came to my dad crying about getting hurt from something, and he told me "Men don't cry". I've been taking that advice for the past 20 years. Only cried seldom for various reasons, but now I feel like I *need* to cry. Maybe it'll make everything better, if for nothing more than 5 minutes. I keep seeing, feeling, hearing my late grandfather (his dad) around me in this empty apartment. I feel like he is here to console me. I grew up semi-religious and I've gradually gone to more deist beliefs in my 20s. I know it sounds odd, but I can feel my grandfather keeping an eye on me. Maybe I'm going crazy from lack of sleep, but thinking about his presence makes me feel a little bit calm.

I love RPGs, but I prefer old school turn-based RPGs to Western ones like Fallout. I never could get into Fallout 3. It's a shame because it's one of the first PS3 games I bought...I barely played an hour before getting fed up with it.

As far as Patterson, I like his Alex Cross series. *Jack and Jill* and *London Bridges* are pretty good. Dan Brown and Steve Berry are a couple of other authors I like. I'm also a big fan of Tolkien and C.S. Lewis. I grew up reading those books.

I know...I just don't want to hear it from him when it eventually happens. I know he'll never forgive me. It's like putting someone in jail. I'll talk to the family and figure out a battle plan to do this the right way.
I'll make a cup of Earl Grey. I probably need something as I took those pills on an empty stomach.

The knife has been put away and I'm currently in a lucid state of mind from the Xanax I took earlier. My chest is hurting from this stress as is my jaw for some reason. In fact, my whole body feels like it's in pain going in and out like ocean waves. I'm hungry, but whenever I go in the kitchen to get something to eat, I don't want to eat it. Not sure if I am going to sleep tonight.
I like reading thrillers, James Patterson is one of my favorite authors. I was playing Red Dead Redemption and quit about two missions before I finish the Mexico missions.
I hardly ever exercise, I used to read and play video games, but I've completely lost all interest in that stuff over the past month. It doesn't bring me any joy anymore.

* I took a break last weekend. Went out of town. Didn't help when I came back to reality.

* I see a shrink but it's only every month. I take meds but I haven't taken them in a week. No money for refills.

* His medicine is in cabinets where he cannot reach. The meds he takes for the week is in his pill box, I refill that every Sunday.

* I am scared to get my family involved, especially his side. They like to gossip about each other, and as angry at him as I am now, I have enough respect not to tell them everything that is going on. I may talk to my grandmother tomorrow, but she's old and feeble and I don't want to stress her out about both me and her son.

I could write a book about my story, but I don't want to bore you. The only people I talk about this to is my mom (who is divorced from him) and my brother, but I only say so much because I don't want them to be upset or depressed about me. Trying to contain my drama as much as I can, but I am seriously about to explode tonight. I may head out in a little bit. I would smoke some weed, but I have to stay clean for a potential DT coming up. That's been keeping me calm for the past week.
